conviction.explanation: Noncash gains representing 51.31% of PBT weaken 8.54x headline cheapness while borrowings rose 29.4% and net debt reached RM21.818bn. CFO improvement is accepted, but acquisitions/expansion still required material net borrowing; the downtrend adds timing risk.

executive_summary:
IOI Properties has improving operations: CFO rose to RM2.391bn from RM1.060bn and left RM1.780bn after specified property/land/equipment outlays before acquisitions and interest. Growing assets can support future recurring income.

The valuation/funding combination remains unfavorable. Fair-value and JV remeasurement gains supplied 51.31% of PBT, so 8.54x trailing earnings is weak recurring-value evidence; forward P/E is 17.71x. Borrowings rose about 29.4%, net debt reached RM21.818bn before leases, and expansion required RM3.258bn net drawdowns. Sell recognizes those costs alongside an unbroken weak price trend.
bull_case: Successful asset lease-up and collections could turn improved CFO into recurring income and eventual deleveraging.
bear_case: Debt-funded expansion and noncash headline profit may mask weaker per-share cash returns; financing exposure can persist even with higher CFO.
key_uncertainties: Recurring profit excluding property/JV valuation gains.
Cash after acquisitions, deposits and interest.
Collection and lease-up timing on the enlarged asset base.
catalysts_upcoming: Positive cash after all specified expansion and interest costs without net borrowing would weaken the financing thesis.
Lower net debt with recurring earnings growth excluding valuation gains would support genuine value compensation.
